scope: Finite source review plus independent CPU unit/mock tests; actual p198 native metadata-tool fixture and adapter qualification remain pending.
resolved_finding: Store snapshot originally accepted stable tensor truncation/extension because neither its inventory nor native metadata mode checked blob extents. Fixed with integer/type validation and stat-size equality for every declared blob, without reading large tensors; regression mocks pass.
reviewed_checks: Explicit known p198 contract selection preserves experimental label and all expected identity fields, including exact engine binary and qualified_by; p181 remains default and unknown contracts refuse.

Policy reserves trusted additional SAVE peak before calling engine; old checkpoint stays charged until successful replacement deletion; detached in-use and ambiguous states retain conservative charges.
Same-ID policy hit re-inspects current identity/prefix and may return existing Parked without SAVE; future adapter must RELEASE any still-pending reply even after a non-None return.
Store accepts only safe native IDs under a fixed real absolute root, checks root/directory inodes, and refuses symlinks/nonregular entries.

Pinned executable is hashed from retained FD and executed through that FD; argv permits only native metadata inspect or native delete with one fixed-root target, never model/device execution arguments.
Snapshot holds native-compatible nonblocking shared sibling flock through native metadata inspection and all small payload reads; lock inode replacement attempts are bounded to three.

Manifest/fields/token/pending reads are bounded; manifest identity/hash, exact closed file set, stable inode/extent/timestamps and declared blob extents checked; storage_bytes includes all regular checkpoint files.
Native inspection remains metadata-only: full tensor hashing/semantic validation is not claimed and native restore must revalidate state.

Delete remains a native-tool operation; success requires typed positive removal receipt and actual absence, in_use requires exact lock refusal, missing is returned only for proven absence; malformed/partial refusal raises.
Timeout applies only to admitted CPU maintenance tool; no model process restart, signal, setting change or recursive Python deletion exists in the store.

save_bound_verification.pooled_rows: N/4 per exact native source; conservative N4096 gives1024 rows

limitations: P198 bridge contract cases use synthetic envelope edits for policy negatives; they do not replace actual native snapshot evidence.
Store runner tests use filesystem/runner mocks and an unexecuted ELF-shaped fixture.
Expected identity, closed loader environment, private root ownership and conservative size bound must come from trusted admission, not an arbitrary checkpoint.
Adapter must validate SAVE snapshot before returning policy metadata, RELEASE on every successful no-SAVE path, and halt rather than release/retry after an ambiguous exception.
